text.p: Springs Industries, a maker of textiles for bed and bath linens and other home furnishings, said Tuesday its fourth-quarter results fell as the company restructured its operations and ran into unexpected problems.

The company, based in Fort Mill, S.C., had earnings of $10.5 million, or 51 cents per share, for the quarter ended Dec. 28, after a $3.19 million charge for the restructuring. In the 1995 period, it earned $26.1 million, or $1.30 a share.
Revenues fell 8 percent to $545.6 million from $593.5 million as a result of the April 1996 sale of the company's Clark-Schwebel subsidiary, it said.
"We were surprised and disappointed by several temporary disruptions which adversely affected our October and November results," Chairman Walter Elisha said.

"These included inefficiencies connected with major systems conversions and with ongoing consolidations of facilities, as well as startup costs incurred to meet certain large orders, most of which will be shipped in the first quarter of 1997," he added.
The company's stock rose 25 cents to $42.25 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
